newsitem.title: USA: International Multifoods targets oper performance.
newsitem.headline: International Multifoods targets oper performance.

text.p: International Multifoods Corp said Wednesday it is taking a series of steps aimed at improving its operating performance and enhancing shareholder value.

These steps include retaining Stern Stewart & Co to help implement economic value added (EVA) to help it assess business unit performance. The company said this effort is aimed at more closely aligning management's interest with those of shareholders.
International Multifoods said it is also completing a thorough strategic review of operations to identify opportunities for profitable growth and significant improvement in EVA.
EVA measures the return on the cost of capital.
Piper Jaffray analyst George Dahlman said the company's plan to implement EVA assessment had been expected as part of its overall efforts to improve performance.
He added the EVA review may result in some divestitures at the company, but did not offer particular examples.
International Multifoods spokeswoman Jill Schmidt, however, said it was too premature to speculate if any divestitures will result from the EVA review.
"The plan right now is to fix and grow the businesses," she added.

The company said it is also launching a program to reduce costs and improve productivity. It established a company-wide procurement task force to identify opportunities to leverage the organization's size and buying power.
International Multifoods said it is also reviewing opportunities to streamline logistics and eliminate related non-value-added activities.

In addition, the company said it is working to reduce working capital and improve asset efficiency to generate additional cash and strengthen its financial position. The company said it initially plans to use excess cash to reduce debt and has targeted at least a $50 million reduction in debt by fiscal 1998 year-end.

"These initiatives represent first steps in our efforts to position the company to deliver sustainable improvements in financial performance and solid returns to shareholders," Chairman Gary Costley said in a statement.
